profile.headline: EDA Tools Software Engineer at Intel Corporation

positions.title: EDA Tools Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Develop Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools for automated generation of CAD designs to be printed onto silicon
- Coordinate definition of high level specs to process and technology-specific designs
- Implement automated checks to ensure process compatibility and signal integrity from tool measurements

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher - Tobias Lab
positions.description:
- Generated atomistic molecular models of the organization and interactions of eye lens proteins and their cataract-related variants
- Identified a cataract-related protein conformation that gives atomistic insight into the "domain-swapping" aggregation mechanism
- Modeled the effects of macromolecular crowding on the conformational dynamics of eye lens proteins.
- Built a molecular dynamics plugin that generates protein structural models consistent with NMR experimental data
- Developed software to calculate drug-membrane permeabilities using Bayesian statistical inference
- Mentored and trained 3 students in performing and analyzing MD simulation data.
- Led discussion sections in graduate and undergraduate level classes in scientific computing, chemical kinetics, and chemistry lab.

positions.title: Contractor - Computational Chemistry
positions.description:
- Developed web apps to predict drug metabolism and reactivity in liver enzymes using computational modeling techniques.
- Provided technical support and write documentation for end users
- Set up and maintained production and development web servers for data analysis pipeline

positions.title: IT Innovation Centre Intern
positions.description:
- Maintained ITIC floor technology
- Conducted floor tours and product demos to ITIC visitors
- Developed and maintained website for ITIC
- Began development on an ITIC robot to automate server equipment inventory procedures

publications.title: Increased hydrophobic surface exposure in the cataract-related G18V variant of human gammaS-crystallin
